issues.legal_issue: The transitional rent-relief provision does not apply to proceedings before the Supreme Court initiated by a petition for special leave, even after special leave is granted.
material_facts: An eviction decree was ultimately founded on the tenants’ non-payment of rent; the grounds of personal requirement and subletting were found unproved.
The decree was upheld in the statutory appellate and revisional proceedings before the tenant sought special leave from the Supreme Court.
The tenant sought the benefit of a later amendment while the special-leave matter was before the Supreme Court, including after special leave had been granted.
issues.conclusion: The amendment’s rent-relief benefit was confined to suits, appeals, and revisions within the statutory hierarchy and did not extend to the special-leave proceeding or the appeal before the Supreme Court. The provision also did not extend to execution proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: The provision’s explanation limits “proceeding” to a suit, appeal, or revision, read with the statutory appeal and revision route in Section 22. The court distinguished a petition for special leave under Article 136 of the Constitution, and the resulting Supreme Court proceeding, from an appeal or memorandum of appeal under the Act: Order XVI Rules 4 and 11 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1966 distinguish the special-leave petition and the appeal after leave, while Order XLI Rule 1(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure requires a memorandum of appeal to state grounds of objection. The court considered that the legislature, presumed aware of Article 136 and the Supreme Court Rules, had not extended the benefit to such proceedings; its limited statutory scope also excluded execution proceedings.

rule.if: rent_eviction_case and statutory_remedies_completed and supreme_court_special_leave_proceeding and tenant_seeks_amendment_relief

predicates.rent_eviction_case: The proceeding concerns eviction of a tenant from rented premises.
predicates.statutory_remedies_completed: The statutory appeal and revision proceedings concerning the eviction decree had concluded before the matter reached the Supreme Court.
predicates.supreme_court_special_leave_proceeding: A party brought the matter before the Supreme Court by seeking special leave, and the Supreme Court proceeding followed that route.
predicates.tenant_seeks_amendment_relief: The tenant sought the benefit of a later amendment while the Supreme Court proceeding was pending.

issues.definition: When a tenant in an eviction case seeks amendment-based rent relief in a Supreme Court special-leave proceeding after the statutory remedies have concluded, that relief is unavailable in that proceeding.
